articles.title: Mikel Arteta’s new contract reflects where the power now lies at Arsenal | Ed Aarons
articles.summary: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club. If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030, just ask Win the dog.
body: Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. But, according to sources close to Win, a therapy dog trained not to bark, there is no contest when it comes to her preferred human: Arteta.

The manager is understood to have taken Win home for Christmas last year, having been instrumental in her arrival a few days after his side had finished as runners-up to Manchester City for the first time. Cuddly replicas are available in the club shop. The real version spends most days at Arsenal’s training centre, with her primary carer a full-time member of staff based there.

“I carefully chose the dog and in my opinion it’s the perfect representative of who we are right now,” said Arteta in 2023. “Win needs accountability from us because we have to look after her as well; her emotions and what she needs.”

articles.title: Women’s Super League faces wait until 2029 for full-time referees despite funding boost
articles.summary: Extra investment agreed at latest WSL board meeting. Calls for fully professional match officials have grown. Women’s Super League clubs have agreed to a major funding increase for match officials but the wait for full-time referees in the English top tier is set to continue until 2029, the…
body: The extra investment, decided at the latest WSL Football board meeting, will focus on enhancing officials’ education, analysis and physical performance, it is understood.

Although none of the parties involved are ruling out progressing to full-time WSL referees earlier, 2029-30 is the campaign that has been agreed for when the officials will be employed by Pro Ref, the official body, formerly known as PGMOL, responsible for match officials across English professional football.

Calls for fully professional WSL match officials have grown since the English women’s top tier became full-time players in 2018-19 and further the top two divisions were taken over by the independent WSL Football in 2024. A further three-year wait is likely to divide opinion.

According to multiple sources, WSL and WSL 2 clubs – the primary shareholders of WSL Football – were told at the all-club meeting this month of the three-year funding plan to transition to full-time match officials for the 2029-30 campaign. Insiders have told the Guardian there was initially a mixed response, with some clubs hoping the move would happen sooner, before the funding plan was voted on and approved.

articles.title: 'Nothing impossible' as NI begin long road to Brazil
articles.summary: Northern Ireland defenders Nat Johnson and Rebecca Holloway tell BBC Sport NI of their dream of reaching a first ever Women's World Cup as NI go through the play-offs.
body: A World Cup staged in Brazil is the stuff of dreams for any footballer and the chance to experience that is on offer for Northern Ireland as they begin their play-off journey against Portugal with hope of securing a spot at next year's tournament.

It will be a difficult ask for Michael McArdle's side, which has been hit by a spate of injuries and features five new faces, but there is a quiet confidence in the group ahead of what will be for some of them, the biggest games in their careers to date.
First up, in what is set to be an arduous journey in search of a World Cup debut, is Friday's home leg at Inver Park (19:30 BST) against the Portuguese.
"When you're growing up, Brazil is the place to be, it's the home of football. It really doesn't get much better than that," said Norwich City defender Natalie Johnson.

articles.title: London Broncos graded below Barrow but still set for Super League place
articles.summary: Championship winners only 16th in new IMG gradings. NRL money contingent on London Super League side. Runaway Championship winners London Broncos have been graded below even Barrow Raiders for next season – but they are still set to become the 15th team in an expanded Super League next season, the…
body: The Broncos have swept aside the second tier in 2026, winning all three domestic trophies on offer after assembling a squad filled with NRL talent. Under the ownership of Kangaroos great, Darren Lockyer, London’s goal was two-fold this year: to dominate on the pitch as well as making a push for the top 14 in the Rugby Football League’s gradings system.

That system determines which teams play in Super League every year, with the highest-ranked 14 clubs across a variety of metrics including attendances, on-field performance and finance being admitted. However, London have finished 16th – below Barrow, who are deemed the best-performing Championship club.

Ordinarily that would mean another season in the Championship, but London look increasingly likely to be given a reprieve. That is because as a partnership between the NRL and Super League nears completion, the Australian governing body has insisted any deal to invest in the British game is conditional on London being in the top flight.

articles.title: Indiana Fever and the Magasphere: a WNBA team’s dangerous path to popularity | Howard Bryant
articles.summary: Teams have always symbolized division within America. And the Fever have come to prominence during a time of dark political intensity. It’s over for now, but no professional sports team spent more time receiving and drawing attention to itself than did the Indiana Fever this season.
body: The Fever were the most polarizing team in professional sports, known less for their basketball than their culpability in pulling the league from its old cultural identity as a Black/queer league into the current ugliness of the Magasphere – a calculated and dangerous path to popularity. There was the basketball of the WNBA, and then there was the Indiana Fever.

Their two most recognizable players, Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham, were in a constant state of churn, always in the news, always embroiled against an other, symbolizing and pandering to America’s fractures. Their best and longest-tenured player, Kelsey Mitchell, hasn’t been able to concentrate fully on basketball the past two seasons as the Clark-Cunningham sideshow devours the oxygen and may end her time in Indiana that began as the second overall pick in 2018.

articles.title: Snakes and jungle mind games as Bottas cycles to Singapore GP
articles.summary: Cadillac driver Valtteri Bottas says he was chased by dogs, saw snakes and leapt over a lizard as he cycled from Malaysia to Singapore for this weekend's Grand Prix.
body: The Finnish driver arrived in Singapore on Wednesday after choosing a 260-mile (419km) bike ride over a flight from last weekend's Formula 1 race in Sepang, outside the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur.
The 37-year-old began his journey just hours after spinning out of Sunday's chaotic Grand Prix, taking a trip that involved off-road and gravel trails as well as cycling at night.
"I saw some snakes, which I was a little bit worried about, but actually they were pretty chill. They were just doing their thing," said Bottas.
"I saw one cobra, one python just crossing the path in front of me. I saw some of those big lizards that you also see here, one was on the path.

articles.title: Afcon final to play out in court - when will Morocco or Senegal be crowned champions?
articles.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport is set to rule on the decision to strip Senegal of their Afcon 2025 title. But fans should not expect an immediate verdict.
body: Everyone knows a football match should take 90 minutes but, in its own way, the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) has been playing out for nearly nine months.
Now, finally, one team or the other - either Morocco or Senegal - willl grab the winner. Only that moment of glory will come in a courtroom, not on the pitch.

On Thursday, Sport's highest legal authority - the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) - will hear Senegal's appeal against the decision to strip them of the title they thought they had won back in January against the hosts in Rabat.
But those hungry for a resolution have already been warned it will not arrive on the same day.

articles.title: Barcelona captain continues to train separately from the squad ahead of Getafe clash
articles.summary: Even as FC Barcelona ramp up their preparations for Saturday’s La Liga clash, there was no change in Raphinha’s situation during their penultimate training session before the return to action following the latest international break.
body: Indeed, according to SPORT, the Brazilian remained in the gym and once again trained separately from the rest of the squad.

He did not take part in Thursday’s group session, which did include the return of the internationals Pau Cubarsi, Rodri, Pedri, Fermin Lopez, Dani Olmo and Lamine Yamal, as well as Anthony Gordon and Dominik Livakovic.

Raphinha left the Brazil camp after suffering a small muscular swelling in the back of his right thigh following the second friendly match against Australia. Medical tests carried out in Barcelona subsequently ruled out an injury.
There had been a possibility that Raphinha would train at the same pace as his teammates for part of Thursday’s session, but he ultimately continued with specific work in the gym.

articles.title: Texas football passed on Jaiden Fields. Now he's slated to chase NFL dream at rival OU
articles.summary: Moments after Jaiden Fields jogged into the end zone for a school-record seventh touchdown, he walked to the Hutto sideline and thanked the linemen, running backs and everyone else with whom he shared the field.
body: "They do a lot for me," the Hippos' standout wide receiver and safety said after last Friday's 68-10 win over Vista Ridge. "Just to be able to tell them I'm thankful and proud of them for being out here and helping me score seven touchdowns (is important)."

Around Hutto, a city of about 46,000, Fields is more than just a catalogue of highlights that wows spectators. A three-star recruit on 247Sports' composite rankings, the two-way star is committed to Oklahoma, where he'll play safety. For now, Fields is a visible, homegrown star who has built a celebrity around town.

Fields is a two-year team captain for Hutto, which is in the hunt for its first outright district championship in nearly a decade. He's been giving tips to younger players and has been a regular at community events. Fans can often find him at middle school games, supporting the same kids who then cheer him on Friday nights, asking the future potential Saturday star for a piece of memorabilia after the game.

"I love it. I love the support," Fields told the American-Statesman in a recent phone interview. "Showing that I'm doing a good thing in the area, just being able to have all these kids look up to me is big."

articles.title: 'Void of leaders' - The problems for bottom-side Spurs after winless start
articles.summary: When Aston Villa went 1-0 up in north London, it felt inevitable that Tottenham would head into the international break winless in the Premier League.
body: That's because it has been nearly two years since Spurs have won a match after conceding the opening goal in any competition. Last month's 3-2 home loss to Villa was the 47th game in this dismal run (D11 L36).
"It is a worry, certainly at home because that's where you need the minerals," former Tottenham boss Tim Sherwood told a special Sky Sports Spurs podcast.
"That's where you need the characters and leaders to come forward, and at the moment, they're void of any leaders and characters.
"I'm not sure there's anyone really losing their head or galvanising the players to try and arrest [it], which is a poor trend, in not fighting back from losing positions.

articles.summary: Arsenal Revive Julian Alvarez Pursuit as Barcelona Doubt Opens January WindowArsenal are back in the frame for Julian Alvarez and, this time, there appears to be a more realistic opening. According to...
body: The key development is straightforward. Alvarez had been set on Barcelona. That preference shaped the market during the summer and, ultimately, blocked Arsenal from making genuine progress. Now, with Barcelona exploring other attacking avenues and uncertainty growing around their capacity to move, Arsenal have been given what the report describes as “fresh hope” that the Argentina international would be prepared to consider North London seriously.

From Arsenal’s perspective, this is not a passing interest. The club were “willing to pay more than £100million for Alvarez” in the summer and held substantial discussions with Atletico. Those talks were not superficial. They involved direct contact between sporting director Andrea Berta and Atletico officials, and they left the relationship between the clubs intact, which matters if the deal is to be revived quickly once the window opens.

articles.title: FIA introducing measures to avoid ‘software bug’ chaos repeat
articles.summary: The FIA will introduce further changes to wet-weather engine software from the United States Grand Prix after completing a review into the "software bug" that further delayed the start of last week's rain-hit race in Malaysia.
body: Several cars slowed or briefly stopped on the rain-hit laps to the grid last Sunday due to what the governing body after the race described as an "unprecedented combination" related to both the slow speed the cars were travelling in the wet and the sector configuration of the Sepang lap.
The start procedure was abandoned and the Grand Prix eventually started 48 minutes later after a software update was issued by the FIA to all teams and power-unit manufacturers.
Having promised an investigation into what happened, the FIA delivered its findings and next steps on Thursday ahead of this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix.

"The review concluded that some cars running on low engine RPM in certain circuit sectors where a 250kW power reduction was applied experienced a loss of power beyond the original intent and that could not be recovered in those sectors," read the statement.

articles.title: Pettersen bounces back on LET return as England's Humphreys moves second
articles.summary: Suzann Pettersen marked her first round on the Ladies European Tour in four years with an even-par 72 at the Aramco Korea Championship as England's Lily May Humphreys earned a share of second place.
body: Pettersen, 45, retired after sinking the winning putt for Team Europe in the 2019 Solheim Cup at Gleneagles, with her only appearance since the 2022 Aramco Team Series event in Jeddah.
The Norwegian - who captained Europe at the 2023 and 2024 Solheim Cups - was three over after six holes in South Korea, bogeying the third and double bogeying the sixth.
But the two-time major winner rallied with birdies at eight, 13 and 15 - picking up a shot at the last of those holes with a monster putt - and went bogey-free on her back nine.
Humphreys - who won her sole Ladies European Tour title to date at the 2023 Joburg Ladies Open - carded a five-under 67 to sit one shot behind leader Patricie Mackova.
